labels.why: Choosing an invocation surface and the context it supplies defines how a Salesforce user asks the bot a question.
Every answer must preserve the asking user's existing record visibility.
The bot must apply existing field permissions and masking rules when reading data and displaying answers.
The specification must identify which callers may use the bot and which may administer it.
Conversation isolation requires an access rule and an explicit decision about administrator access.
The transaction constraints determine where the asynchronous callout belongs in the bot's execution flow.
The integration needs a secure location for the credential and a rule that keeps it out of logs and source.
The applicable timeout, callout count, heap and CPU ceilings constrain what each bot job can do.
A mock callout lets the Apex tests exercise the integration under the runtime's test restrictions.
Registering the endpoint is a deployment prerequisite for the bot's callout to succeed.
The interface needs a delivery mechanism for an answer that arrives after the initiating transaction.
A retry must preserve the one-reply-per-request rule.
The queue or concurrency ceiling determines when the bot must handle an enqueue failure.
The interface needs distinct outcomes for provider refusal, server failure and timeout.
The bot needs a recovery and feedback policy for provider throttling or exhausted quota.
A partial answer and an absent answer require distinguishable outcomes for the user.
A persistent transcript schema with model and usage metadata adds a record store to a bot that can answer without it.
Conversation data needs a retention period and a removal policy covering expiry and user deletion.
The prompt policy must identify eligible org data and the treatment of personal data within the caller's access rights.
The context size at which the bot trims or summarises history determines how it handles long conversations.
First use and empty questions need explicit handling, as do questions and answers at the length ceiling.
Operators need visibility into failed requests, while turning the bot off and switching models add administrator controls.
Audit data needs a retention period, while storing the full question and answer for audit adds a transcript store.
Environment-specific credentials, configuration and deployment steps make the bot reproducible in the target org.
The answer-time target sets a measurable bound, and the interface needs to show when a reply is still pending.
The bot interface must distinguish an empty conversation, a pending answer, an error and a refusal.
Installing the bot must preserve existing sharing, records and automation.
The main decision is how an open spot becomes a booking, with an acceptance deadline if an offer is used.
Promotion requires an ordering rule that resolves ties and says whether priority exceptions exist.
Promoting someone into one class must reconcile their overlapping waitlist entry to avoid a booking conflict.
The existing penalty policy needs to identify which declined or missed promotions count against a member.
The booking flow needs a background trigger that starts promotion promptly after a cancellation.
A promoted member needs notice through a chosen channel, with defined handling if delivery fails.
Concurrent openings must preserve class capacity and prevent duplicate promotions.
A direct booking racing with a promotion needs one consistent booking outcome.
A promotion into a paid class must integrate with charging and resolve a failed payment.
A maximum queue length determines when another member cannot join and what they see.
The promotion deadline defines how close to class start an opening can still be offered.
Capacity increases and decreases require distinct handling of waiting members and available spots.
Cancelling the class requires a disposition for everyone still waiting.
Serving the queue requires an entry representation that supports ordering and tracks each member's status.
Past entries need a post-class disposition and a retention period.
The waitlist must protect other members' identities, while displaying an exact queue position adds a member-facing feature.
Staff queue views, manual promotion and removal, and a promotion history add management features.
Global and per-class switches add configuration controls beyond joining and serving a waitlist.
The maximum delay from cancellation to promotion defines how quickly an available spot must be used.
The waitlist must preserve direct booking for available classes and honour existing reservations.
Rollout needs a rule for joining the waitlist of a class that was already full.
The number of sends and their due-date offsets define when reminders start, recur and end.
The scheduler must identify every invoice state that stops further reminders.
A reminder for a partially paid invoice needs a rule for which balance it displays.
The sender must distinguish customer contact restrictions and identify which ones suppress a billing notice.
Retries, deployments and concurrent schedulers must preserve one send per reminder step.
Rechecking payment status immediately before sending prevents a stale reminder.
Failed delivery requires a recovery path and a person responsible for persistent failures.
Batch pacing must respect the provider's sending-rate ceiling.
Activation needs a backlog policy so overdue invoices do not trigger every missed send at once.
Local sending hours define a time window, and weekends and holidays require an eligibility rule.
The amount and currency must be rendered unambiguously for the recipient.
Bounced addresses, invalid addresses and missing contacts need explicit delivery outcomes.
Recipient eligibility must identify which billing contacts receive a reminder when several are on file.
The sender needs a per-step delivery record for tracing and deduplication, while displaying it on the invoice adds a view.
The message needs accurate invoice and payment details and a decision about the validity of any payment link.
The specification must identify who may configure the schedule, while manual sending and stopping add separate reminder controls.
Global and customer switches, interactive previews and manual resends add operator controls to the automatic sequence.
Operators need to see delivery failures for follow-up, while a view of upcoming sends adds a preview feature.
A volume ceiling or maximum lateness defines a measurable boundary for scheduled delivery.
Adding reminder delivery must preserve the existing invoice creation, payment and recording flows.
The importer needs a transaction policy that tells admins whether valid rows survive another row's failure.
A row-level result lets the admin identify failed user creations and their causes.
Matches against existing users and duplicates within the upload are distinct conflict cases.
Each imported role assignment must preserve the importing admin's authority boundary.
The specification must identify which admins have bulk-import permission independently of single-user creation.
File validation must identify required columns and distinguish unknown columns, missing columns and absent headers.
The parser contract must cover encoding and line-ending variants as well as quoted separators and newlines.
A late row failure needs a recovery rule that accounts for invitations already sent for earlier rows.
The upload needs a byte or row ceiling and a defined outcome for oversized files.
Empty, header-only and single-row inputs are distinct cases whose outcomes the importer must define.
Repeated uploads need a consistent rule for preventing or explaining repeated effects.
Background processing needs a completion signal so the admin can obtain the import outcome.
Bulk creation must define the sending pace if the existing user workflow issues invitations or welcome mail.
Creating a usable account requires an initial status, credential policy and path through the existing sign-in flow.
Personal data needs secure handling and a retention period, while re-downloading an upload adds a retrieval feature.
The import contract needs an unambiguous parsing rule for dates and numbers across locales.
An audit record makes bulk account creation traceable to the initiating admin and import time.
Cancelling a running job and selectively retrying failed rows add separate job-management actions.
A maximum-size upload needs a completion-time bound and progress feedback during processing.
Bulk creation must preserve manual account creation and the contents of existing user records.
Formula-like values require safe result rendering, and overlength fields must be handled at the destination column's size limit.
